blocks.text: Good to know about Fairfield Island

items.t: There are no SnapStats numbers for Fairfield Island — anyone quoting one is quoting nothing.

"Island" is a local name with no published boundary in the sources checked. The City plans the area (Schedule B2, with Chilliwack Proper) but the research could not verify its exact boundaries or dike geography on an official source — treat any precise boundary line in listing copy as UNVERIFIED.

A detached house here can still come with a strata fee. The Williams Road example sits in a 6-unit bare-land strata described in its listing as carrying a minimal fee — a buyer who assumes "detached = no strata" misses the corporation, its bylaws and its Form B entirely.

The flood question is open, not answered — and that is the point. Unlike areas where this series could cite a floodplain bylaw position, Fairfield Island's dike and flood-construction-level facts stayed UNVERIFIED all the way through the research (City sources blocked, 429). A seller's reassurance is not a substitute for the City's own parcel check.

The plan pairing surprises people: Fairfield Island is not planned on its own — its neighbourhood plan is the joint Schedule B2 "Chilliwack Proper and Fairfield Island Neighbourhoods Plan," so plan searches run under only "Fairfield Island" miss documents filed under Chilliwack Proper.

Provincial dates that changed a bare-land strata lot's rule book here: rental bylaws void November 24, 2022; wider 55+ exemptions May 1, 2023; 10% CRF minimum November 1, 2023; depreciation reports every five years from July 1, 2024; Chilliwack SSMUH Bylaw 5395 adopted June 18, 2024.

items.t: Why this section still matters with zero stock: Pure fee-simple detached purchases have no Form B; diligence runs on title, permits and the flood/ALR checks below instead.

Chilliwack property taxes (city ground only): notices are mailed at the end of May and taxes are due the first working day after July 1; a 5% penalty applies to taxes outstanding after July 2, 2026 and an additional 5% to taxes outstanding after August 4, 2026. Fairfield Island is inside the City of Chilliwack, so the city scheme applies — the FVRD electoral-area rural regime (Taxation (Rural Area) Act s. 11, 5% after July 2 + 5% after Oct 31) does NOT apply here; never mix the two.

blocks.text: Good to know about Fairfield Island

items.t: The "island" is a slough, not the Fraser River, that makes it an island in daily life. The Schedule B-2 plan states Fairfield Island is separated from the rest of Chilliwack Proper by the Hope Slough, is currently accessible only via road bridges at Menzies and Young Roads, and will add a planned pedestrian and cyclist bridge at Williams Street — every trip to the hospital and the downtown stock crosses one of those two bridges.

The plan expects infill, not a townhouse project. The Schedule B-2 framework addresses infill development opportunities — redevelopment of existing large lots into smaller-lot single detached, duplex or row housing, some convenience commercial, and new attached housing along Hope River Road — and notes there are limited commercial services within the neighbourhood at present. No townhouse complex for Fairfield Island appears in any source checked.

Fairfield Island's housing era is stated in the City's own plan. The Schedule B-2 plan characterises the current building stock as predominantly one- and two-storey 1970s–1980s detached homes — a buyer here is buying a house of that era, with a house inspection to match, not a strata purchase with a depreciation report.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect land buyers in Fairfield Island

items.t: SSMUH / suites / accessory dwellings (Chilliwack specifics): the SSMUH amendment is ESTABLISHED — Zoning Bylaw Amendment Bylaw 2024, No. 5395 amended Zoning Bylaw 2020, No. 5000 and was adopted June 18, 2024, as recorded in s. 14's amendment record in the consolidated Zoning Bylaw 5000 ( item 6). Suite/ADU figures confirmed in the same verification (item 7f, citing Zoning Bylaw 5000, ss. 2, 4.06, 5.04): a secondary suite is capped at the lesser of 90 m² and 40% of the principal dwelling, one accessory dwelling unit is permitted per lot, garden suites are capped at 100 m², and parking rules sit at s. 5.04. Application to any specific parcel remains a per-parcel check.

ALR block — full form (the northern/eastern perimeter where ALR ground exists): properties in the Agricultural Land Reserve are subject to the Agricultural Land Commission Act and ALR regulations; ALC approval may be required before the City can approve related development applications, and the City directs owners to check ALR status on the City Webmap; an ALC application may be required for a new house, coach house or suite, for placing fill or removing soil, for non-farm uses, and for subdivision or a boundary adjustment, with ALC applications referred to the City for review. Subdivision within the ALR requires ALC approval, and ALR residences cannot be stratified (ALC Information Bulletin 09, s. 6; Strata Property Act, s. 239; Agricultural Land Commission Act, s. 21(1)). Residence caps: principal residence ≤500 m² total floor area; a secondary suite only inside the principal residence; one additional residence capped at 90 m² on parcels of 40 ha or less and 186 m² on parcels over 40 ha. Farm Home Plate: OCP Development Permit Area 4 exists to reduce the long-term impact of residential uses on agricultural land, and a Development Permit is required when the Zoning Bylaw's Farm Home Plate regulations are not met. Farm class (BC Assessment) in full three-tier form: $2,500 of gross farm income on 0.8–4 ha; $2,500 plus 5% of the actual value of the area over 4 ha above that; $10,000 under 0.8 ha — applications by October 31. A flat "$2,500+" line is an ERROR and is not used here.

: Form B (SPA s. 123.1/123.2 + May 1, 2023 exemptions); a "45+" listing line is NOT a valid BC age bylaw. Pure freehold detached purchases have no Form B; diligence runs on title, permits and the flood/ALR checks instead.

Speculation and vacancy taxes: no speculation- or vacancy-tax position for a Fairfield Island parcel is documented in this area's research — none is imported. Vancouver's Empty Homes Tax at 3% is VANCOUVER ONLY and does not apply here.

The neighbourhood plan is shared, not standalone. Fairfield Island has no plan of its own: it is planned jointly with Chilliwack Proper as Schedule B2 of Bylaw 5500 — a buyer reading only a "Fairfield Island plan" would be reading the wrong document.

faq.q: Who can help me buy or sell in Fairfield Island?
faq.a: Jared Gibbons, REALTOR® with Royal LePage Little Oak Realty, works across the Fraser Valley and Metro Vancouver. Call or text 604-928-1361 or use the contact form on this site.

faq.q: How do I find out which school serves an address in Fairfield Island?
faq.a: School catchments are set by address, so use the school district's catchment locator with the exact address. Catchment lines change, so check before you write an offer.

faq.q: Do I need a home inspection when buying in Fairfield Island?
faq.a: It is strongly recommended. Make the offer subject to an inspection so a qualified inspector can look at the roof, structure, drainage, electrical and heating before you remove conditions.

faq.q: Can I book a private showing with Jared?
faq.a: Yes. Jared Gibbons, REALTOR® with Royal LePage Little Oak Realty, books private showings across the Fraser Valley and Metro Vancouver. Call or text 604-928-1361, or use the contact form on this site.

faq.q: Are there any apartment condos on Fairfield Island?
faq.a: The confirmed stock is detached houses (some on bare-land strata lots) and perimeter acreages.

It is a residential neighbourhood in the City of Chilliwack north of Chilliwack Proper, working to Young Road North, Menzies Road, Hope River Road, Clare Avenue, Bell Road and Ballam Road, and it is planned together with Chilliwack Proper under Schedule B2 of the City's Official Community Plan.

faq.q: A Fairfield Island listing says "strata" — is that a condo?
faq.a: Not necessarily. If a lot is bare-land strata there IS a strata corporation, with fees and bylaws; the strata plan's first page is what settles it.

faq.q: Can ALR rules affect a Fairfield Island property?
faq.a: They can where a parcel is in the Agricultural Land Reserve — the northern and eastern perimeter acreages are the exposure. ALR properties are subject to the Agricultural Land Commission Act and regulations, and an ALC application may be required for a new house, coach house or suite, fill or soil removal, a non-farm use, or a subdivision or boundary adjustment; check a parcel on the City Webmap. An ALR residence also cannot be stratified.

faq.q: Can a Fairfield Island house add a suite or a second unit?
faq.a: Within the city-wide rules: a secondary suite is capped at the lesser of 90 m² and 40% of the principal dwelling, one ADU is permitted per lot, and garden suites are capped at 100 m² (Zoning Bylaw No. 5000, ss. 2, 4.06, 5.04); the SSMUH amendment (Bylaw 5395, adopted June 18, 2024) is the separate added-unit route for eligible parcels. Per-parcel eligibility: UNVERIFIED — confirm with the City. ( item 7f)

faq.q: Are there any townhouses on Fairfield Island?
faq.a: The confirmed stock is detached houses (some on bare-land strata lots) and perimeter acreages.

faq.q: A Fairfield Island listing says "strata" — is that a townhouse?
faq.a: Not on the verified example. The Williams Road example is a detached single-family house on a 6-unit bare-land strata (title: Freehold Strata; sub-type: Single Family Residence) — a strata lot carrying a house, not a unit in a townhouse complex. If a lot is bare-land strata there IS a strata corporation, with fees and bylaws; the strata plan's first page is what settles it.

It is a residential neighbourhood in the City of Chilliwack north of Chilliwack Proper, north of the Hope Slough per the Schedule B-2 plan, working to Young Road North, Menzies Road, Hope River Road, Clare Avenue, Bell Road and Ballam Road, and planned together with Chilliwack Proper under Schedule B2 of the City's OCP.
